explanation: 'Eighth' counts the notes of a scale such as C major, from C up to the next C. Counting each step between neighbouring keys, black ones included, gives 12. Each octave up doubles the frequency.

claims.text: An octave does not span 7, 8 or 10 semitones.
Octave comes from the Latin for eighth, because in a major scale the octave note is the eighth, counting the starting note.
From one C to the next on a piano, every step between neighbouring white and black keys is a semitone, making 12 in all.
Raising a note by an octave doubles its frequency.
